content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

Explain the structure of DNA as a polymer

are polymers that occur in living organisms. They include proteins, carbohydrates (starch and cellulose), and DNA. These polymers are essential for life and are formed by condensation reactions, just like synthetic condensation polymers.
Proteins are made from amino acids:
R is a variable side chain (different for each amino acid)

This continues to form a polypeptide chain

Explain how proteins are formed from amino acids.
Amino acids have two functional groups:
Carboxylic acid group (-COOH) at the other end
The -COOH of one amino acid reacts with the -NH₂ of another
A water molecule is released (condensation reaction)
A peptide bond (-CONH-) forms between the amino acids
A long polypeptide chain is formed
The sequence of amino acids determines the protein's properties
